solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Soup prepared for work

indicators.note: food that is prepared is made up from its ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A bowl of soup being made ready to serve at the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' is the anagram signal applied to SOUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer's or writer's numbered piece is called an opus, Latin for a piece of work.

clue.text: Respect always joining queen and English

parts.note: R is short for regina, Latin for queen
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: Deference to the monarch and the English nation as a permanent duty.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere someone is to hold them in deep respect or awe; both are verbs of esteem.

clue.text: Give up something to plant, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word for the planted thing is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a seed is what a gardener puts in the soil

explanation.surface: Abandoning a gardening plan, giving up something meant for planting.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede territory or a point is to surrender or yield it to another.

clue.text: Politician's quality says chap's fashionable

parts.note: states means says, as in 'he states his case'
a chap is a man, so chap's gives man's
hip means trendy or fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a fellow's statecraft is very much in vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill in managing public affairs wisely is the hallmark of a leader of real stature in government.

clue.text: Desert creature with trouble lifting evergreen shrub

parts.note: the camel is the classic animal of the desert

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting raises a word upward, so the word for trouble reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, as in 'what ails you?'

explanation.surface: A camel struggling to raise a bush in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'lifting' means the word is written bottom to top in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The camellia is a glossy-leaved ornamental bush of the tea family that keeps its foliage all year.

clue.text: An area under prohibition for fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue being under means placed below, so these pieces come after the other one

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: A region subject to a ban on fruit imports.
explanation.definitionFit: The banana is a familiar long yellow tropical fruit, a straightforward example.

clue.text: Need gear to move rat

indicators.note: letters made to move change position, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Equipment is required to shift a rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rat' looks like the rodent but is a verb-turned-noun for a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat in slang is a betrayer or deserter, just as a renegade abandons a cause.

clue.text: General rule in doorstep receptions

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the phrase that follows, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A general rule of etiquette for greeting guests at the front door.
explanation.definitionFit: A precept is a guiding principle or maxim meant to regulate conduct.

clue.text: Humble sailor, like slave, ultimately

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a crossword staple for a sailor
as means like, as in 'white as snow'

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of the word slave is used

explanation.surface: A lowly seaman treated like a slave in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To humble someone, used as a verb, is to lower or degrade them, the same as debasing them.

clue.text: A lot of Cologne, perhaps has European landscape

indicators.note: a lot of but not all, so the last letter of the scent word is dropped

parts.note: eau de cologne is an example of a scent

explanation.surface: Much of the German city of Cologne has a European look to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cologne' seems to be the city but is the perfume; 'A lot of' drops the final T of SCENT, leaving SCEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene is a view or vista, the stretch of country one looks out over.

clue.text: Support old horse, note, quite young

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
a nag is an old or worn-out horse
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Backing an elderly horse, a reminder says it is actually fairly young.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in their teens is fairly young, between child and adult.

clue.text: Unity over five points

parts.note: on means over or upon, as in 'on the table'
five compass points: east, north, east, south, south

explanation.surface: Agreement reached after discussing five key points.
explanation.definitionFit: Oneness is the state of being whole and undivided, a synonym of unity.

clue.text: Astonished old writer spotted

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
eyed means looked at or spotted

explanation.surface: An elderly author has been sighted, to everyone's amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wide-eyed with surprise, staring in wonder, is how an astonished person looks.

clue.text: Redesigned tech site is visually pleasing to Americans

indicators.note: something redesigned is put together afresh, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A technology website's makeover looks good to American users.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to Americans' points to the US spelling without the A of aesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Esthetic is the American spelling of an adjective describing beauty or artistic taste.

clue.text: Beast of burden carrying large Tibetan priest

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the priest word wraps round the size letter

parts.note: a lama is a Buddhist monk of Tibet
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A pack animal bearing a hefty Himalayan monk.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American animal long used to carry loads, a classic pack animal.

clue.text: Apply authority without power

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for power is removed

parts.note: an authority on a subject is an expert
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Wielding control without any real strength behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert pressure or influence is to bring it to bear, to apply it.

clue.text: Former husband quiet with increase

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
and means together with

explanation.surface: An ex-husband keeping quiet as his wealth grows.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand is to grow larger, a verb meaning to swell or enlarge.

clue.text: Some esteemed a Cambridge backing the scholarly world

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters found are read right to left
some means just part, so the letters are taken from within these words

explanation.surface: Respected figures at a Cambridge college supporting academic life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes EMEDACA from inside 'esteemed a Cambridge' and 'backing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the realm of universities and learning, named after Plato's Academy.

clue.text: One or the other solvent absorbs iodine

indicators.note: absorbs means takes in, so the solvent word goes round the element letter

parts.note: ether is a volatile liquid used as a solvent
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about which liquid takes up iodine.
explanation.definitionFit: Either refers to one of two options, whichever is chosen.

clue.text: Former news media, say

parts.note: ex means former
the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: Newspapers of the past, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a thought is to put it into words, to state or utter it.

clue.text: Old-fashioned beer brought back without pressure

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for pressure is removed
brought back means returned, so the beer word is written in reverse

parts.note: porter is a dark beer
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A traditional ale is revived, served without being pumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' gives RETROP; 'without' then drops its P.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro describes a style deliberately imitating past fashions, so a dated look.

clue.text: A lot of paper's pale yellow with no carbon

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the letter for carbon is taken away

parts.note: cream is a pale yellowish-white colour
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A big stack of cream-coloured paper with no carbon copies.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a bundle of 500 sheets, a large quantity of stationery.

clue.text: Variety of agate needs working unknown times

parts.note: on means working, as with a switched-on machine
Y is an algebraic unknown
X is the multiplication sign

explanation.surface: A gemmologist's note that a type of stone takes endless working.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded chalcedony, a kind of the striped quartz mineral.

clue.text: Tedium starts to exhaust now nothing usually interests

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Boredom wears you out when nothing grabs your attention any more.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French-derived word for listless boredom and weariness.

clue.text: Ridiculously, any line is wrong

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of place, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that some line of text is absurdly incorrect.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanely means in a silly, senseless way, an adverb like foolishly.
